# Your page on GitHub

---

## The goal

A long-term personal page, public, at

`https://<user-name>.github.io`

- free: no server to buy or to manage
- the content is Markdown/HTML/CSS 
- every change you *commit* or push from your computer goes online by itself

---

## GitHub Pages

GitHub can *serve* the files of a repository as a web site

There are two kinds of site:

- **user site**: the repo is called `<user-name>.github.io` --> `https://<user-name>.github.io`

- **project site**: any other repo, e.g., `my-repo` --> `https://<user-name>.github.io/my-repo`

. . .

Today: the user site. The name of the repository is the magic word.

---

## Example

Compare 

  - source: [github.com/ale66/ale66.github.io](https://github.com/ale66/ale66.github.io){target="_blank"}, and
    
  - rendering: [ale66.github.io](https://ale66.github.io){target="_blank"}  


---

## Lab experience

0. sign in, go to your GH profile

1. create the repository, add a minimal web page

2. publish the repo, check it on github.io 

3. from your computer, `git clone` and start work


# Step by step

---

## 1. Create the repository

1. sign in to [github.com](https://github.com) and click **New repository**

2. *Repository name*: exactly `<user-name>.github.io`

3. choose **Public**

4. tick *Add a README file*

5. click **Create repository**

. . .

Careful: your exact user name + `.github.io`

`ale66` --> `ale66.github.io`

---

## 1. Create the repository

![](./imgs/new-repo.png)

---

## 2. A first page

In the new repository: **Add file** --> **Create new file**

name it `index.html`

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>My first page</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Hello, I am <user-name></h1>
  <p>This is my page on GitHub.</p>
</body>
</html>
```

then **Commit changes**

---

## Why `index.html`?

When nobody asks for a specific file, the server delivers `index.html`

- `https://<user-name>.github.io` --> `index.html`

- `https://<user-name>.github.io/about.html` --> `about.html`


---

## 3. Switch on publishing

**Settings** --> **Pages**

- *Source*: **Deploy from a branch**
- *Branch*: `main`, folder `/ (root)`
- click **Save**

. . .

If Pages is already active then we're done.

![](./imgs/pages-settings.png)

---

## 4. Visit your page

1. open the **Actions** tab: a job called *pages build and deployment* runs

2. wait for the green tick (a minute or two)

3. go to `https://<user-name>.github.io`

. . .

Not there yet? See *When it does not work*, a few slides ahead.

---

## What just happened

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[edit] --> B[commit]
  B --> C[GH builds the site]
  C --> D[GH publish on github.io]
```

Every commit on the `main`branch repeats the cycle.

# Editing

---

## Option A: in the browser

- open the file in the repository
- click the pencil icon
- change the text, then **Commit changes**

Quick fixes, no installation.

---

## Option B: with VS Code

Clone the repo to your computer and work as usual

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<user-name>/<user-name>.github.io.git
```

Open the folder in VS Code, edit, save. Then publish the changes:

```bash
git status # are all changes good?
git add .
git commit -m "update my page"
git push
```


# Markdown

---

Thanks to automated Pandoc interpretation, GH can render and publish at once


Replace `index.html` with `index.md`

```markdown
# Hello, I am <user-name>

This is my page on GitHub.

- [About me](about.html)
- [My projects](projects.html)
```

GitHub renders it into HTML and sends it to `github.io`

. . .

Keep *one* of the two, `index.html` or `index.md`, not both.

---

## A site with several pages

```
<user-name>.github.io/
├── index.html
├── about.html
├── style.css
└── imgs/
    └── me.png
```

links use *relative* paths:

- `<a href="about.html">About</a>`
- `![](./imgs/me.png)`
- `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">`


# Potential Issues

## Unreachable

`404`: page not found

- typos in the repo name
- the repo is not **Public**
- there is no `index.html` (nor `index.md`) in the root folder

. . .

the page is old: wait a minute, then reload without cache (`Ctrl+Shift+R`)

. . .

images are missing: `Me.png` is not `me.png`, check upper/lower case and the path

. . .

a red cross in the **Actions** tab: open it and read the message

---

## Issues around publishing

All-or-nothing: public is universal

private repos can have collaborators

- no phone number, home address, ID documents, passwords...
  
- no pictures of other people without their consent

  - the version history is public too: deleted files are still visible in earlier commits.

# Summary of the method

---

- a repository called `<user-name>.github.io` is published as the web site `https://<user-name>.github.io`

- the repository must be public

- `index.html` (or `index.md`) is the front door

- Settings --> Pages: deploy from the `main` branch

- every commit is online within minutes

- edit from the browser, or clone and use VS Code with `git add`, `commit`, `push`

---

## Self-assessment

- what must the repository be called, and why?

- what is `index.html` for?

- what happens when you commit a change to `main`?

- where do you look when your page shows a `404`?

- what should you *not* publish on a public page?

---

## Coda: more sites from one account

Any other repository can be published too, as a *project site*

`https://<user-name>.github.io/my-repo`

Same recipe: **Settings** --> **Pages** --> `main`

Your user site can link to all of them.

---
